subject: Compact on-prem VPC architecture review for edge inference deployment
messages:

Subject: Compact on-prem VPC architecture review for edge inference deployment

Hi all,

Attached is an initial compact VPC proposal for EdgeCorp's on-prem inference footprint. The ask from the field is to keep the packaging small (single 1U appliance per site), minimize egress, and preserve control-plane observability back to Redwood for metrics/alerts while satisfying their compliance team.

Key constraints:
- Single NIC per appliance preferred (networking simplicity for ops)
- No persistent public IPs assigned to tenant plane
- Telemetry (metrics/traces) must be able to reach our SaaS control plane but routed through EdgeCorp's proxy
- Multitenant isolation at network boundary without full overlay for performance reasons

What I want from this thread: rapid architecture sanity-check and a short list of constraints we can't bend on, plus any immediate red flags (BGP/NAT hairpinning, telemetry batching, egress proofing).

Included attachments: compact-vpc-sketch.pdf, egress-policy-matrix.csv

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Compact on-prem VPC architecture review for edge inference deployment

Thanks Marissa — good concise brief. A few initial technical observations (high level):

1) Single-NIC appliance: OK if we push more responsibility to EdgeCorp's border. We will need strong iptables rules plus policy-based routing to avoid tenant traffic egressing into management plane. If EdgeCorp insists on a single VLAN for tenant and mgmt, we'll want hardware-enforced VRF or host-level namespace enforcement.

2) Control-plane telemetry: prefer an egress-only tunnel from the appliance to Redwood control plane (TLS over mTLS) using port 443 and relying on EdgeCorp's outbound proxy. Make sure we support connection backoff and local buffering (1GB) for telemetry in case proxy is intermittent.

3) Multitenancy at boundary: instead of overlay, propose per-tenant L3 prefixes with strict prefix-list + per-tenant iptables chains to guarantee no cross-tenant forwarding. This reduces CPU/latency vs overlay, but requires ops discipline on prefix allocation.

4) BGP/NAT: if they want active-active border, we should avoid exposing private tenant IPs via BGP to public. NAT at the border for any external reachability is essential. Watch out for hairpin NAT when two tenants communicate via public endpoints — document the expected behavior.

Action items from me: I'll annotate the sketch with a per-plane IP assignment and suggested iptables rules.

-Jonas
Lead Infrastructure Architect

From: Eli Santos <eli.santos@edgepartners.io>

Subject: Re: Compact on-prem VPC architecture review for edge inference deployment

Marissa, team — thanks for the draft. A couple of practical notes from EdgePartners/EdgeCorp ops:

- EdgeCorp's proxy enforces domain allowlists; we need a precise FQDN list for telemetry and control-plane endpoints and a fallback that uses an enterprise relay if the proxy denies direct traffic.
- Many of their sites only allow ephemeral outbound connections (idle timeout ~5m). Does Redwood implement keepalive and reconnect with jitter?
- On NAT: they prefer 1:1 SNAT for customer egress so logs map cleanly to tenant. That means our appliance must annotate sessions with tenant IDs or use source tagging upstream.

I'll loop in a site ops engineer for a quick validation call if you want.

—Eli
EdgePartners Solutions

Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compact on-prem VPC architecture review for edge inference deployment

Adding practical details and a small canary plan. I've attached a canary-routing-diagram.png and an egress-policy-matrix.csv that maps expected traffic flows to allowed FQDNs. Highlights:

- Telemetry buffering: implement a local circular buffer with checkpointing to disk and exponential backoff. If buffered >80% capacity, drop low-priority telemetry (traces) and preserve metrics/alerts.
- Connectivity checks: health pings to control-plane with 3s interval, 3 retries, then escalate to site sysadmin.
- Canary: roll to 5 non-critical sites with slightly more permissive egress to test hostname allowlist and reconnection behavior. After 7 days, evaluate packet drop and control-plane sync lag.

Proposed iptables snippets (in attachment) and a short runbook:
- pre-routing: mark tenant packets, do per-tenant prerouting rules
- nat: SNAT to border-managed 1:1 IP mapping

Can we lock the FQDN list next week? I will submit a sanitized list for compliance to review.

Mina 
Senior Field Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Compact on-prem VPC architecture review for edge inference deployment

Appreciate the quick turn. Summary and next steps:

Summary decisions:
- Single NIC OK with host-level isolation + iptables VRF-like rules.
- Telemetry will go out via EdgeCorp proxy (allowlist); Redwood will support TLS+mTLS, buffering with priority drop, and connection jitter/backoff.
- Use border NAT (1:1 SNAT) for any external reachability; appliance will tag sessions to preserve tenant identity in logs.
- No overlay; per-tenant L3 prefixes with prefix lists and policy enforcement.

Next steps:
- Mina: share the sanitized FQDN allowlist by EOD Mon 2029-04-15 (for compliance).
- Jonas: drop-in the iptables rule examples into the draft sketch and flag any kernel/module dependencies.
- EdgeCorp ops (ops@edgecorp.com): confirm proxy idle-timeout behavior and whether they can bump to 15m during canary.
- Schedule a 30-minute validation call next Wed; calendar invite to follow.

I'll update the Drive folder with the annotated sketch and runbook. Thanks everyone — good progress.

Marissa
